subject: Request: compliance pack & processor-chain details for international transfer review
messages:
From: Eli Barnes <eli@trustgrid.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance pack request for our legal review

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security and procurement teams are running an international transfer review for a pilot with Redwood and need a few items to complete their assessment. Can you send a single packet that contains: a processor-chain map showing all subprocessors (including cloud regions used in APAC), a current signed DPA or the template DPA you propose, PCI/SOC evidence summary (SOC 2 Type II report summary is fine), and a short note on how customer KMS/HSM keys and logs are handled for cross-border contracts?

We have a deadline to complete the review by May 20. If you can provide the packet and indicate whether Redwood will accept an Art. 28 clause with the standard UK Addendum for transfers, that would be ideal.

Also, procurement may ask for an export of Art. 30 ledger entries relevant to our account (data categories processed, subprocessors, and retention policies) — is that something you can produce?

Best,
Eli Barnes
Head of Procurement, TrustGrid
eli@trustgrid.com

--
Eli Barnes
TrustGrid

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Eli Barnes <eli@trustgrid.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance pack request for our legal review

Hi Eli —

Thanks — we can absolutely assemble a consolidated compliance pack. I'll put together a processor-chain map and a draft DPA (with the UK Addendum options) and include a SOC 2 summary and a short note about key management and audit logging.

Two quick clarifications so we provide exactly what you need:
- For the Art. 30 ledger export, do you need a CSV of ledger entries filtered to your account only, or a redacted example ledger plus a statement of procedures?
- For KMS: do you want our typical flow where customer keys are optional (bring-your-own-key) with envelope encryption, or do you need a formal KMS attestation for your platform security team?

I'll loop in Legal and Privacy (cc'd) to confirm our DPA stance and to prepare the processor-list export. Expect an initial packet by EOD Wednesday (May 12). If procurement needs DocuSign for the DPA, we can generate an envelope.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachments: (none in this message)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Eli Barnes <eli@trustgrid.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance pack request for our legal review

Stephanie / Eli —

I've prepared the draft DPA and a processor-chain diagram for APAC. A few legal points for procurement to note (I'll add these as a cover memo in the packet):
1) Subprocessor list: our primary subprocessors for APAC are AWS (ap-southeast-1), GCP (asia-east1) for backups, and Fastly for CDN edge caching. We also use a third-party telemetry provider (TelemetryCo) for anonymized performance metrics.
2) Transfer safeguards: we support SCCs where required and a UK Addendum. For customers requiring additional contractual guarantees we offer tailored transfer annexes; those require legal review and may take 7–10 business days.
3) Art. 30 export: We can produce a CSV that includes timestamped ledger entries scoped to the customer account (data categories, subprocessors invoked, retention policy field). We will redact internal-only operational notes.
4) Key management: Redwood supports BYOK via customer KMS (AWS KMS + external HSM integrations). When BYOK is used we store only envelope keys in our vault; raw key material remains with the customer's KMS. We can provide a technical attestation describing the envelope workflow and rotation cadence.

Eli — I attached the draft DPA (redwood-dpa-v4.docx) and a processor map (redwood-processor-map-apac-2027.pdf) as a starting point. I flagged two clauses where procurement often requests edits: liability cap carve-outs for security incidents and a subsection on subcontractor audits. If TrustGrid needs an audit ride-along or a SOC 2 bridge letter, we can coordinate with Compliance.

Markus
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-dpa-v4.docx, redwood-processor-map-apac-2027.pdf
